# ureq - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ureq/^2/

## Expand description

A simple, safe HTTP client.

[!NOTE]

- 2.12.x is MSRV 1.71
- 2.11.x is MSRV 1.67
For both these lines, we will release patch version pinning dependencies as needed to retain the MSRV. If we are bumping MSRV, that will require a minor version bump.

[!NOTE] ureq version 2.11.0 was forced to bump MSRV from 1.63 -> 1.67. The problem is that the

`time`crate 0.3.20, the last 1.63 compatible version, stopped compiling with Rust[1.80 and above](https://github.com/algesten/ureq/pull/878#issuecomment-2503176155). To release a 2.x version that is possible to compile on the latest Rust we were forced to bump MSRV.

Ureq’s first priority is being easy for you to use. It’s great for
anyone who wants a low-overhead HTTP client that just gets the job done. Works
very well with HTTP APIs. Its features include cookies, JSON, HTTP proxies,
HTTPS, interoperability with the `http` crate, and charset decoding.

Ureq is in pure Rust for safety and ease of understanding. It avoids using
`unsafe` directly. It [uses blocking I/O](https://docs.rs#blocking-io-for-simplicity) instead of async I/O, because that keeps
the API simple and keeps dependencies to a minimum. For TLS, ureq uses
[rustls or native-tls](https://docs.rs#https--tls--ssl).

See the [changelog](https://github.com/algesten/ureq/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for details of recent releases.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

In its simplest form, ureq looks like this:

```
fn main() -> Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    let body: String = ureq::get("http://example.com")
        .set("Example-Header", "header value")
        .call()?
        .into_string()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
For more involved tasks, you’ll want to create an [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.Agent.html). An Agent
holds a connection pool for reuse, and a cookie store if you use the
“cookies” feature. An Agent can be cheaply cloned due to an internal
[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html) and all clones of an Agent share state among each other. Creating
an Agent also allows setting options like the TLS configuration.

```
  use ureq::{Agent, AgentBuilder};
  use std::time::Duration;
  let agent: Agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
      .timeout_read(Duration::from_secs(5))
      .timeout_write(Duration::from_secs(5))
      .build();
  let body: String = agent.get("http://example.com/page")
      .call()?
      .into_string()?;
  // Reuses the connection from previous request.
  let response: String = agent.put("http://example.com/upload")
      .set("Authorization", "example-token")
      .call()?
      .into_string()?;
```
Ureq supports sending and receiving json, if you enable the “json” feature:

```
  // Requires the `json` feature enabled.
  let resp: String = ureq::post("http://myapi.example.com/post/ingest")
      .set("X-My-Header", "Secret")
      .send_json(ureq::json!({
          "name": "martin",
          "rust": true
      }))?
      .into_string()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

ureq returns errors via `Result<T, ureq::Error>`. That includes I/O errors,
protocol errors, and status code errors (when the server responded 4xx or
5xx)

```
use ureq::Error;
match ureq::get("http://mypage.example.com/").call() {
    Ok(response) => { /* it worked */},
    Err(Error::Status(code, response)) => {
        /* the server returned an unexpected status
           code (such as 400, 500 etc) */
    }
    Err(_) => { /* some kind of io/transport error */ }
}
```
More details on the [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) type.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

To enable a minimal dependency tree, some features are off by default. You can control them when including ureq as a dependency.

`ureq = { version = "*", features = ["json", "charset"] }`

- `tls`enables https. This is enabled by default.
- `native-certs`makes the default TLS implementation use the OS’ trust store (see TLS doc below).
- `cookies`enables cookies.
- `json`enables- [Response::into_json()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.into_json)and- [Request::send_json()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_json)via serde_json.
- `charset`enables interpreting the charset part of the Content-Type header (e.g.- `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=iso-8859-1`). Without this, the library defaults to Rust’s built in- `utf-8`.
- `socks-proxy`enables proxy config using the- `socks4://`,- `socks4a://`,- `socks5://`and- `socks://`(equal to- `socks5://`) prefix.
- `native-tls`enables an adapter so you can pass a- `native_tls::TlsConnector`instance to- `AgentBuilder::tls_connector`. Due to the risk of diamond dependencies accidentally switching on an unwanted TLS implementation,- `native-tls`is never picked up as a default or used by the crate level convenience calls (- `ureq::get`etc) – it must be configured on the agent. The- `native-certs`feature does nothing for- `native-tls`.
- `gzip`enables requests of gzip-compressed responses and decompresses them. This is enabled by default.
- `brotli`enables requests brotli-compressed responses and decompresses them.
- `http-interop`enables conversion methods to and from- `http::Response`and- `http::request::Builder`(v0.2).
- `http`enables conversion methods to and from- `http::Response`and- `http::request::Builder`(v1.0).

[§](https://docs.rs#plain-requests)Plain requests

Most standard methods (GET, POST, PUT etc), are supported as functions from the
top of the library ([get()](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html), [post()](https://docs.rs/fn.post.html), [put()](https://docs.rs/fn.put.html), etc).

These top level http method functions create a [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) instance
which follows a build pattern. The builders are finished using:

- `.call()`
- `.send()`- [Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)(chunked encoding support for non-known sized readers).
- `.send_string()`
- `.send_bytes()`
- `.send_form()`

[§](https://docs.rs#json)JSON

By enabling the `ureq = { version = "*", features = ["json"] }` feature,
the library supports serde json.

- `request.send_json()`
- `response.into_json()`

[§](https://docs.rs#content-length-and-transfer-encoding)Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding

The library will send a Content-Length header on requests with bodies of
known size, in other words, those sent with
[ .send_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_string),

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_bytes)

`.send_bytes()`[, or](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_form)

`.send_form()`[. If you send a request body with](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_json)

`.send_json()`[, which takes a](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send)

`.send()`[Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)of unknown size, ureq will send Transfer-Encoding: chunked, and encode the body accordingly. Bodyless requests (GETs and HEADs) are sent with

[and ureq adds neither a Content-Length nor a Transfer-Encoding header.](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.call)

`.call()`If you set your own Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header before sending the body, ureq will respect that header by not overriding it, and by encoding the body or not, as indicated by the headers you set.

```
let resp = ureq::post("http://my-server.com/ingest")
    .set("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
    .send_string("Hello world");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#character-encoding)Character encoding

By enabling the `ureq = { version = "*", features = ["charset"] }` feature,
the library supports sending/receiving other character sets than `utf-8`.

For [ response.into_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Response.html#method.into_string) we read the
header

`Content-Type: text/plain; charset=iso-8859-1` and if it contains a charset
specification, we try to decode the body using that encoding. In the absence of, or failing
to interpret the charset, we fall back on `utf-8`.Similarly when using [ request.send_string()](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html#method.send_string),
we first check if the user has set a

`; charset=<whatwg charset>` and attempt
to encode the request body using that.[§](https://docs.rs#proxying)Proxying

ureq supports two kinds of proxies,  [ HTTP](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Proxy_servers_and_tunneling#http_tunneling) (

[),](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/CONNECT)

`CONNECT`[and](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCKS#SOCKS4)

`SOCKS4`[, the former is always available while the latter must be enabled using the feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCKS#SOCKS5)

`SOCKS5``ureq = { version = "*", features = ["socks-proxy"] }`.Proxies settings are configured on an [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.Agent.html) (using [AgentBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBuilder.html)). All request sent
through the agent will be proxied.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-using-http)Example using HTTP

```
fn proxy_example_1() -> std::result::Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    // Configure an http connect proxy. Notice we could have used
    // the http:// prefix here (it's optional).
    let proxy = ureq::Proxy::new("user:password@cool.proxy:9090")?;
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .proxy(proxy)
        .build();
    // This is proxied.
    let resp = agent.get("http://cool.server").call()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-using-socks5)Example using SOCKS5

```
fn proxy_example_2() -> std::result::Result<(), ureq::Error> {
    // Configure a SOCKS proxy.
    let proxy = ureq::Proxy::new("socks5://user:password@cool.proxy:9090")?;
    let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
        .proxy(proxy)
        .build();
    // This is proxied.
    let resp = agent.get("http://cool.server").call()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#https--tls--ssl)HTTPS / TLS / SSL

On platforms that support rustls, ureq uses rustls. On other platforms, native-tls can
be manually configured using [ AgentBuilder::tls_connector](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBuilder.html#method.tls_connector).

You might want to use native-tls if you need to interoperate with servers that only support less-secure TLS configurations (rustls doesn’t support TLS 1.0 and 1.1, for instance). You might also want to use it if you need to validate certificates for IP addresses, which are not currently supported in rustls.

Here’s an example of constructing an Agent that uses native-tls. It requires the “native-tls” feature to be enabled.

```
  use std::sync::Arc;
  use ureq::Agent;
  let agent = ureq::AgentBuilder::new()
      .tls_connector(Arc::new(native_tls::TlsConnector::new()?))
      .build();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#trusted-roots)Trusted Roots

When you use rustls (`tls` feature), ureq defaults to trusting
[webpki-roots](https://docs.rs/webpki-roots/), a
copy of the Mozilla Root program that is bundled into your program (and so won’t update if your
program isn’t updated). You can alternately configure
[rustls-native-certs](https://docs.rs/rustls-native-certs/) which extracts the roots from your
OS’ trust store. That means it will update when your OS is updated, and also that it will
include locally installed roots.

When you use `native-tls`, ureq will use your OS’ certificate verifier and root store.

[§](https://docs.rs#blocking-io-for-simplicity)Blocking I/O for simplicity

Ureq uses blocking I/O rather than Rust’s newer [asynchronous (async) I/O](https://rust-lang.github.io/async-book/01_getting_started/02_why_async.html). Async I/O
allows serving many concurrent requests without high costs in memory and OS threads. But
it comes at a cost in complexity. Async programs need to pull in a runtime (usually
[async-std](https://github.com/async-rs/async-std#async-std) or [tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio#tokio)). They also need async variants of any method that might block, and of
[any method that might call another method that might block](https://journal.stuffwithstuff.com/2015/02/01/what-color-is-your-function/). That means async
programs usually have a lot of dependencies - which adds to compile times, and increases
risk.

The costs of async are worth paying, if you’re writing an HTTP server that must serve
many many clients with minimal overhead. However, for HTTP *clients*, we believe that the
cost is usually not worth paying. The low-cost alternative to async I/O is blocking I/O,
which has a different price: it requires an OS thread per concurrent request. However,
that price is usually not high: most HTTP clients make requests sequentially, or with
low concurrency.

That’s why ureq uses blocking I/O and plans to stay that way. Other HTTP clients offer both an async API and a blocking API, but we want to offer a blocking API without pulling in all the dependencies required by an async API.

Ureq is inspired by other great HTTP clients like
[superagent](http://visionmedia.github.io/superagent/) and
[the fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API).

If ureq is not what you’re looking for, check out these other Rust HTTP clients:
[surf](https://crates.io/crates/surf), [reqwest](https://crates.io/crates/reqwest),
[isahc](https://crates.io/crates/isahc), [attohttpc](https://crates.io/crates/attohttpc),
[actix-web](https://crates.io/crates/actix-web), and [hyper](https://crates.io/crates/hyper).

# uuid - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/uuid/^1/

## Expand description

Generate and parse universally unique identifiers (UUIDs).

Here’s an example of a UUID:

`67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8`A UUID is a unique 128-bit value, stored as 16 octets, and regularly formatted as a hex string in five groups. UUIDs are used to assign unique identifiers to entities without requiring a central allocating authority.

They are particularly useful in distributed systems, though can be used in disparate areas, such as databases and network protocols. Typically a UUID is displayed in a readable string form as a sequence of hexadecimal digits, separated into groups by hyphens.

The uniqueness property is not strictly guaranteed, however for all practical purposes, it can be assumed that an unintentional collision would be extremely unlikely.

UUIDs have a number of standardized encodings that are specified in [RFC 9562](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc9562.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#getting-started)Getting started

Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
# Lets you generate random UUIDs
features = [
    "v4",
]
```
When you want a UUID, you can generate one:

```
use uuid::Uuid;
let id = Uuid::new_v4();
```
If you have a UUID value, you can use its string literal form inline:

```
use uuid::{uuid, Uuid};
const ID: Uuid = uuid!("67e55044-10b1-426f-9247-bb680e5fe0c8");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#working-with-different-uuid-versions)Working with different UUID versions

This library supports all standardized methods for generating UUIDs through individual Cargo features.

By default, this crate depends on nothing but the Rust standard library and can parse and format UUIDs, but cannot generate them. Depending on the kind of UUID you’d like to work with, there are Cargo features that enable generating them:

- `v1`- Version 1 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v3`- Version 3 UUIDs based on the MD5 hash of some data.
- `v4`- Version 4 UUIDs with random data.
- `v5`- Version 5 UUIDs based on the SHA1 hash of some data.
- `v6`- Version 6 UUIDs using a timestamp and monotonic counter.
- `v7`- Version 7 UUIDs using a Unix timestamp.
- `v8`- Version 8 UUIDs using user-defined data.

This library also includes a [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) type that can be used to help construct UUIDs of any
version without any additional dependencies or features. It’s a lower-level API than

[that can be used when you need control over implicit requirements on things like a source of randomness.](https://docs.rs/struct.Uuid.html)

`Uuid`[§](https://docs.rs#which-uuid-version-should-i-use)Which UUID version should I use?

If you just want to generate unique identifiers then consider version 4 (`v4`) UUIDs. If you want
to use UUIDs as database keys or need to sort them then consider version 7 (`v7`) UUIDs.
Other versions should generally be avoided unless there’s an existing need for them.

Some UUID versions supersede others. Prefer version 6 over version 1 and version 5 over version 3.

[§](https://docs.rs#other-features)Other features

Other crate features can also be useful beyond the version support:

- `serde`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `serde`.
- `borsh`- adds the ability to serialize and deserialize a UUID using- `borsh`.
- `arbitrary`- adds an- `Arbitrary`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for fuzzing.
- `fast-rng`- uses a faster algorithm for generating random UUIDs when available. This feature requires more dependencies to compile, but is just as suitable for UUIDs as the default algorithm.
- `rng-rand`- forces- `rand`as the backend for randomness.
- `rng-getrandom`- forces- `getrandom`as the backend for randomness.
- `bytemuck`- adds a- `Pod`trait implementation to- `Uuid`for byte manipulation

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

Some features are unstable. They may be incomplete or depend on other unstable libraries. These include:

- `zerocopy`- adds support for zero-copy deserialization using the- `zerocopy`library.

Unstable features may break between minor releases.

To allow unstable features, you’ll need to enable the Cargo feature as
normal, but also pass an additional flag through your environment to opt-in
to unstable `uuid` features:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg uuid_unstable"`[§](https://docs.rs#building-for-other-targets)Building for other targets

[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly)WebAssembly

For WebAssembly, enable the `js` feature:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
features = [
    "v4",
    "v7",
    "js",
]
```
[§](https://docs.rs#embedded)Embedded

For embedded targets without the standard library, you’ll need to
disable default features when building `uuid`:

```
[dependencies.uuid]
version = "1.23.4"
default-features = false
```
Some additional features are supported in no-std environments:

- `v1`,- `v3`,- `v5`,- `v6`, and- `v8`.
- `serde`.

If you need to use `v4` or `v7` in a no-std environment, you’ll need to
produce random bytes yourself and then pass them to [ Builder::from_random_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.from_random_bytes)
without enabling the

`v4` or `v7` features.If you’re using `getrandom`, you can specify the `rng-getrandom` or `rng-rand`
features of `uuid` and configure `getrandom`’s provider per its docs. `uuid`
may upgrade its version of `getrandom` in minor releases.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Parse a UUID given in the simple format and print it as a URN:

```
let my_uuid = Uuid::parse_str("a1a2a3a4b1b2c1c2d1d2d3d4d5d6d7d8")?;
println!("{}", my_uuid.urn());
```
Generate a random UUID and print it out in hexadecimal form:

```
// Note that this requires the `v4` feature to be enabled.
let my_uuid = Uuid::new_v4();
println!("{}", my_uuid);
```

# tonic_build - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tonic-build/^0.12/

## Expand description

`tonic-build` compiles `proto` files via `prost` and generates service stubs
and proto definitions for use with `tonic`.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

- `cleanup-markdown`: Enables cleaning up documentation from the generated code. Useful when documentation of the generated code fails- `cargo test --doc`for example.
- `prost`: Enables usage of prost generator (enabled by default).
- `transport`: Enables generation of- `connect`method using- `tonic::transport::Channel`(enabled by default).

[§](https://docs.rs#required-dependencies)Required dependencies

```
[dependencies]
tonic = <tonic-version>
prost = <prost-version>
[build-dependencies]
tonic-build = <tonic-version>
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Simple

```
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    tonic_build::compile_protos("proto/service.proto")?;
    Ok(())
}
```
Configuration

```
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
   tonic_build::configure()
        .build_server(false)
        .compile_protos(
            &["proto/helloworld/helloworld.proto"],
            &["proto/helloworld"],
        )?;
   Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nixos-related-hints)NixOS related hints

On NixOS, it is better to specify the location of `PROTOC` and `PROTOC_INCLUDE` explicitly.

```
$ export PROTOBUF_LOCATION=$(nix-env -q protobuf --out-path --no-name)
$ export PROTOC=$PROTOBUF_LOCATION/bin/protoc
$ export PROTOC_INCLUDE=$PROTOBUF_LOCATION/include
$ cargo build
```
The reason being that if `prost_build::compile_protos` fails to generate the resultant package,
the failure is not obvious until the `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/resultant.rs"));`
fails with `No such file or directory` error.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- Service code generation for client
- [manual](https://docs.rs/manual/index.html)
- This module provides utilities for generating `tonic`service stubs and clients purely in Rust without the need of`proto`files. It also enables you to set a custom`Codec`if you want to use a custom serialization format other than`protobuf`.
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- Service code generation for Server

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Attributes](https://docs.rs/struct.Attributes.html)
- Attributes that will be added to `mod`and`struct`items.
- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)- `prost`
- Service generator builder.
- [Code](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeGenBuilder.html)- GenBuilder
- Builder for the generic code generation of server and clients.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html)- `prost`
- Configuration options for Protobuf code generation.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileDescriptorSet.html)- Descriptor - Set - `prost`
- The protocol compiler can output a FileDescriptorSet containing the .proto files it parses.

# spanda_sdk - Rust

## Expand description

Official Rust SDK for Spanda — thin HTTP client over Control Center API v1.

Core platform logic lives in Rust runtime crates; this crate delegates to
`spanda-api` REST endpoints without duplicating business rules.

Enable feature `grpc` for a native tonic client.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/spanda-sdk/0.5.5/src/spanda_sdk/lib.rs.html

# spanda_sdk/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Official Rust SDK for Spanda — thin HTTP client over Control Center API v1.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Core platform logic lives in Rust runtime crates; this crate delegates to
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! `spanda-api` REST endpoints without duplicating business rules.
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! Enable feature `grpc` for a native tonic client.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)
[8](https://docs.rs#8)pub mod client;
[9](https://docs.rs#9)pub mod error;
[10](https://docs.rs#10)pub mod stream;
[11](https://docs.rs#11)pub mod types;
[12](https://docs.rs#12)
[13](https://docs.rs#13)#[cfg(feature = "grpc")]
[14](https://docs.rs#14)pub mod grpc;
[15](https://docs.rs#15)
[16](https://docs.rs#16)pub use client::{AuthConfig, SpandaClient, SpandaClientBuilder};
[17](https://docs.rs#17)pub use error::SpandaError;
[18](https://docs.rs#18)pub use stream::EventStream;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)pub use types::*;
[20](https://docs.rs#20)
[21](https://docs.rs#21)#[cfg(feature = "grpc")]
[22](https://docs.rs#22)pub use grpc::GrpcClient;

pub struct EventStream {
    pub ws_url:
```

}## Expand description

WebSocket telemetry stream handle.

Connect to `WS /v1/stream/telemetry` on the Control Center server.
Full streaming requires an async runtime; use language-specific SDKs
(Python `TelemetryStream`, TypeScript `EventStream`) for production use.

# spanda_sdk::client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/spanda-sdk/0.5.5/spanda_sdk/client/index.html

# sim_codec - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-codec/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Core decoder/encoder and output-position contracts for the SIM codec layer.

sim-codec is the foundation crate of the sim-codec-* family. The SIM kernel
defines the `Expr` graph and the codec contract types; this crate provides
the concrete runtime that every other codec crate implements against: the
`Decoder`/`Encoder` traits, their located and tree-shaped variants, the
`DecodePosition`/`DecodeTarget` output-position model (eval, quote, data,
pattern), and the `CodecRuntime` glue that registers a codec as a
runtime object. On top of those contracts it carries the shared
`Expr`<->tree encode machinery, domain-codec scaffolding, decode resource
limits, portable encode/decode, string-literal coding, and tree validation.

A decoder turns tokens or text into a checked `Expr` form; an encoder knows
its output position and renders an `Expr` back to text or bytes. Downstream
crates (general-purpose and domain codecs) build on these primitives rather
than re-implementing them.

Module map (these modules are private; their public items are re-exported at the crate root, so they are listed here in plain text rather than linked):

- implementation: implementation root that aggregates the submodules below
and re-exports their public surface.
- runtime: the `Decoder`/`Encoder`runtime contracts, the`DecodePosition`/`DecodeTarget`output positions,`Input`/`Output`, and the`CodecRuntime`registration glue.
- domain: builder scaffolding for domain codec libs (`DomainCodecLib`) and the shared UTF-8 input helper.
- domain_form: a generic `#(...)`domain-form parser and formatter.
- limits: decode resource ceilings (`DecodeLimits`), running budgets (`DecodeBudget`), and the`ReadCx`decode context.
- list_encode: the shared list/`Expr`value-to-expr encode machinery.
- portable: codec-neutral, lossless portable encode/decode for the data
subset of `Expr`.
- strings: string-literal encode/decode helpers.
- tree: structural validation of a `LocatedExprTree`.

- runtime: the
- runtime_api: the eval-facing surface that drives codecs through the kernel
(`DecodedForm`, codec lookup, and decode/encode entry points).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Codec](https://docs.rs/struct.CodecRuntime.html)- Runtime
- A registered codec as a runtime object: a symbol-named bundle of optional decode/encode capabilities plus the Shapes and default-decode policy it exposes.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeBudget.html)- Budget
- Running counters for a single decode. Construct one per decode call.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeLimits.html)- Limits
- Resource ceiling shared by every codec decode path.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainCodecLib.html)- Codec - Lib
- A host-registered lib that exports one codec (and optionally the Shapes it uses) built from a decoder and encoder.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainForm.html)- Form
- A parsed `#(name ...)`form: a name, keyed fields, and positional values.
- [Loss](https://docs.rs/struct.LossReport.html)- Report
- Loss report for one parse/encode/reparse cycle.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- A parse diagnostic surfaced by the Prism.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismEncode.html)- Encode
- Encode result for one codec surface.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismInspection.html)- Inspection
- Metadata describing how input was inspected.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismParse.html)- Parse
- Parse result for one codec surface.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismSpan.html)- Span
- A half-open byte span belonging to a parsed surface.
- [ReadCx](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadCx.html)
- The decode context threaded through every `Decoder`
- [Round](https://docs.rs/struct.RoundTrip.html)- Trip
- Full round-trip proof for one codec surface.
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/struct.RuntimeCodecPrism.html)- Codec - Prism
- Runtime-backed `CodecPrism`
- [Semantic](https://docs.rs/struct.SemanticId.html)- Id
- Stable identity for a semantic expression.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binary](https://docs.rs/enum.BinaryCarrier.html)- Carrier
- How binary frame bytes are carried at the codec boundary.
- [Codec](https://docs.rs/enum.CodecDefaultDecode.html)- Default - Decode
- A codec’s policy for choosing a `DecodeTarget``DecodePosition`

- The syntactic position a decode is targeting, mirroring the kernel’s
`EncodePosition`.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeTarget.html)- Target
- The checked form a decode resolves to once a position is known: inert data or an evaluable term.
- [Decoded](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodedForm.html)- Form
- The position-resolved result of a default decode: inert data or an evaluable term.
- [Diagnostic](https://docs.rs/enum.DiagnosticSeverity.html)- Severity
- Diagnostic severity.

- A parsed domain-form value.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.Input.html)
- Raw input handed to a `Decoder`

- Rendered output produced by an `Encoder`

- What kind of input the Prism inspected.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/enum.PrismOutput.html)- Output
- Output from a Prism encode pass.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/enum.PrismSurface.html)- Surface
- The class of codec surface a Prism is driving.

- The core decode contract: turn `Input``Expr`.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html)
- The core encode contract: render a kernel `Expr`to`Output`

- An encoder that consumes a `LocatedExpr``Encoder`
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/trait.TreeDecoder.html)- Decoder
- A decoder that preserves the full source tree as a `LocatedExprTree`
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/trait.TreeEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder that consumes a full `LocatedExprTree`

- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_value_expr.html)- value_ - expr
- Walk a runtime `Value`into a kernel`Expr`ready for encoding.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_value_with_codec.html)- value_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a runtime `Value`with the codec named`symbol`, forcing lists and tables into an`Expr`via`encode_value_expr`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_with_codec.html)- with_ - codec
- Encode `expr`with the codec named`symbol`under`options`.
- [force_](https://docs.rs/fn.force_list_for_encode.html)- list_ - for_ - encode
- Force a list value into a bounded Vec for v1 encoding.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/fn.format_domain_form.html)- domain_ - form

- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_domain_form.html)- domain_ - form
- Parse a top-level `#(...)`domain form.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_expr_shape.html)- expr_ - shape
- Resolve a general codec’s expression shape: the `primary`symbol, then`core/Expr`, then`core/Any`, then nil. This is the shared fallback chain that every general-purpose codec (json/binary/binary-base64/algol/lisp/doc) hand-rolled identically before OVERLAP6.07.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_options_shape.html)- options_ - shape
- Resolve a general codec’s encode-options shape: `core/EncodeOptions`, then`core/Any`, then nil. The shared fallback chain those codecs hand-rolled.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_expr_tree.html)- expr_ - tree
- Check that a `LocatedExprTree``Expr`.

# sim_kernel - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

sim-kernel is the small protocol kernel of the SIM Rust runtime.

The kernel defines contracts; libraries supply behavior. This crate holds
the protocol and contract types – forms, values, stores, registry and
callable surfaces, the [ shape](https://docs.rs/shape/index.html) protocol, evaluation policy, and the ABI
transport – while concrete behavior (parsers, number domains, the standard
distribution, and server/agent/browse implementations) lives in separate
library crates loaded against these contracts. SIM is a Rust runtime, not a
Lisp runtime; Lisp is one codec surface among several.

The one deliberate exception is the pair of built-in *reference backends*:
[ list::VecList](https://docs.rs/list/struct.VecList.html) (a

[) and](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListValue.html)

`list::ListValue`[(a](https://docs.rs/table/struct.AssocTable.html)

`table::AssocTable`[). These are the kernel’s bootstrap list and table implementations – minimal, correct, and self-annotated](https://docs.rs/table/trait.Table.html)

`table::Table``sim-non-citizen` –
so the runtime can stand up collections before any library loads. They are
reference implementations, not the only backends: alternatives load as libs
against the [/](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListBackend.html)

`list::ListBackend`[contracts. (Future cleanup: move even these into a default-loaded distribution lib so the kernel ships pure contracts; tracked against the constellation reorg.)](https://docs.rs/table/trait.TableBackend.html)

`table::TableBackend`The kernel data flow is:

`tokens -> checked forms -> objects -> checked calls -> objects -> encoded forms`[§](https://docs.rs#module-map)Module map

Core forms and values: [ value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/expr/index.html)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [callable](https://docs.rs/callable/index.html)
- The callable contract: objects that can be invoked with checked arguments.

# sim_lib_binding - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-binding/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Binding behavior for the SIM runtime: lexical, dynamic, and scoped binding.

The kernel defines the binding-related contracts; this crate supplies the concrete binding organ (lexical/letrec scopes, dynamic parameters, modes).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/struct.BindingProfileModes.html)- Profile - Modes
- The binding and hygiene modes selected for a language profile.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.rs/struct.DynamicEnv.html)- Env
- A stack of dynamic-extent binding frames shared across clones.
- [Lexical](https://docs.rs/struct.LexicalEnv.html)- Env
- A lexical scope: a frame of name-to-value slots chained to its parent.
- [Lexical](https://docs.rs/struct.LexicalFunction.html)- Function
- A closure that captures a `LexicalEnv`
- [Parameter](https://docs.rs/struct.Parameter.html)
- A dynamic parameter: a named fluid binding with a fallback default.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/enum.BindingScopeMode.html)- Scope - Mode
- How a language profile scopes its bindings.
- [Hygiene](https://docs.rs/enum.HygieneMode.html)- Mode
- How a language profile treats macro hygiene.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [RECIPES](https://docs.rs/static.RECIPES.html)
- Cookbook recipes for the binding organ, embedded at build time.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_dynamic_let_op_key.html)- dynamic_ - let_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `dynamic-let`form (dynamic-extent binding).
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_let_op_key.html)- let_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `let`form (parallel lexical binding).
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_let_star_op_key.html)- let_ - star_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `let*`form (sequential lexical binding).
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_letrec_op_key.html)- letrec_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `letrec`form (mutually recursive lexical binding).
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_op_keys.html)- op_ - keys
- All operation keys contributed by the binding organ, in claim order.
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_organ_symbol.html)- organ_ - symbol
- Symbol identifying the binding organ in the claim store.
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_parameterize_op_key.html)- parameterize_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `parameterize`form (dynamic parameter rebinding).
- [binding_](https://docs.rs/fn.binding_profile_modes_op_key.html)- profile_ - modes_ - op_ - key
- Operation key for the `profile-modes`form (per-profile binding/hygiene modes).
- [eval_](https://docs.rs/fn.eval_let.html)- let
- Evaluates a `let`form: parallel bindings in a fresh child scope.
- [eval_](https://docs.rs/fn.eval_let_star.html)- let_ - star
- Evaluates a `let*`form: sequential bindings in a fresh child scope.
- [eval_](https://docs.rs/fn.eval_letrec.html)- letrec
- Evaluates a `letrec`form: mutually recursive bindings in a child scope.
- [lexical_](https://docs.rs/fn.lexical_function_value.html)- function_ - value
- Wraps a `LexicalFunction``Value`
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_binding_organ_claims.html)- binding_ - organ_ - claims
- Publishes the binding organ’s claims and operation keys into a `Cx`
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_binding_organ_claims_for_lib.html)- binding_ - organ_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes binding organ claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/type.BindingInitializer.html)- Initializer
- Computes a binding’s initial value within a (possibly partial) scope.

# sim_lib_control - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-control/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Control behavior for the SIM runtime: async, backtracking, conditions.

The kernel defines the control-policy contracts; this crate supplies the concrete control organ (coroutines, generators, restarts, non-local exits) layered over those contracts.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncTask.html)- Task
- A deterministic async task that resolves after a fixed number of polls.
- [Backtracker](https://docs.rs/struct.Backtracker.html)
- A linear backtracking choice point over a fixed list of alternatives.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html)
- A signalled condition: a kind symbol plus a payload reference.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionHandler.html)- Handler
- A handler bound to a condition kind, prompt, and capture continuation.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionStack.html)- Stack
- A stack of `ConditionHandler`
- [Continuation](https://docs.rs/struct.ContinuationValue.html)- Value
- A runtime object wrapping a captured continuation and its capture result.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlFunction.html)- Function
- A callable runtime object exposing one control primitive.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlLib.html)- Lib
- The control organ as a loadable kernel `Lib`
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlResultValue.html)- Result - Value
- A runtime object wrapping the result reference of a control operation.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlTag.html)- Tag
- Stable tag identifying a delimited control prompt.
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/struct.Coroutine.html)
- Two cooperating value streams that yield by alternating between lanes.
- [Generator](https://docs.rs/struct.Generator.html)
- A single-lane generator that yields a fixed sequence of values on demand.
- [Labeled](https://docs.rs/struct.LabeledPrompt.html)- Prompt
- A labeled escape target: a label symbol bound to a control prompt.
- [NonLocal](https://docs.rs/struct.NonLocalExit.html)- Exit
- A pending non-local exit: a kind, a target label, and a carried value.
- [OneShot](https://docs.rs/struct.OneShotControlPolicy.html)- Control - Policy
- A control policy that allows each captured continuation to resume once.
- [Restart](https://docs.rs/struct.Restart.html)
- A named recovery point: a symbol bound to a captured continuation.
- [Restart](https://docs.rs/struct.RestartStack.html)- Stack
- A stack of `Restart`
- [Segmented](https://docs.rs/struct.SegmentedControlPolicy.html)- Control - Policy
- A one-shot control policy scoped to a named delimited segment.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/enum.AsyncPoll.html)- Poll
- Outcome of polling an `AsyncTask`
- [Backtrack](https://docs.rs/enum.BacktrackStep.html)- Step
- Result of advancing a `Backtracker`
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/enum.CoroutineLane.html)- Lane
- Identifies which of a coroutine’s two cooperating lanes yielded a value.
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/enum.CoroutineStep.html)- Step
- Outcome of resuming a `Coroutine`
- [Generator](https://docs.rs/enum.GeneratorStep.html)- Step
- Outcome of advancing a `Generator`
- [NonLocal](https://docs.rs/enum.NonLocalExitKind.html)- Exit - Kind
- The flavor of a non-local exit: loop break, loop continue, or block return.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Control](https://docs.rs/trait.ControlPrompt.html)- Prompt
- Library-level contract for prompts raised by runtime organs.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [abort_](https://docs.rs/fn.abort_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/abort`symbol.
- [capture_](https://docs.rs/fn.capture_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/capture`symbol.
- [control_](https://docs.rs/fn.control_exports.html)- exports
- Returns the lib’s exported `control/*`functions as kernel`Export`
- [control_](https://docs.rs/fn.control_op_keys.html)- op_ - keys
- Returns the standard control operation keys this organ claims:
`prompt`,`capture`,`abort`, and`resume`.
- [control_](https://docs.rs/fn.control_organ_symbol.html)- organ_ - symbol
- Returns the `organ/control`symbol identifying this control organ.
- [escape_](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_to_label.html)- to_ - label
- Performs `exit`by aborting to the matching`LabeledPrompt``prompts`.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_control_lib.html)- control_ - lib
- Installs the control organ into `cx`: loads`ControlLib`
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_control_policy.html)- control_ - policy
- Installs the default `one_shot_control_policy``cx`as the active control policy.
- [invoke_](https://docs.rs/fn.invoke_restart.html)- restart
- Invokes the restart named `name`on`stack`with`value`; free-function form of`RestartStack::invoke`
- [manifest_](https://docs.rs/fn.manifest_name.html)- name
- Returns the `sim/control`manifest id under which this lib registers.
- [one_](https://docs.rs/fn.one_shot_control_policy.html)- shot_ - control_ - policy
- Builds a shared `OneShotControlPolicy``ControlPolicyRef`
- [prompt_](https://docs.rs/fn.prompt_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/prompt`symbol.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_control_organ_claims.html)- control_ - organ_ - claims
- Publishes the control organ’s claims into `cx`, recording that this organ supplies the standard`control_op_keys``control_organ_symbol`
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_control_organ_claims_for_lib.html)- control_ - organ_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes control organ claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.
- [raise_](https://docs.rs/fn.raise_prompt.html)- prompt
- Raises a library-level control prompt through the kernel control contract.
- [resume_](https://docs.rs/fn.resume_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/resume`symbol.
- [segmented_](https://docs.rs/fn.segmented_control_policy.html)- control_ - policy
- Builds a shared `SegmentedControlPolicy``segment`as a kernel`ControlPolicyRef`
- [signal_](https://docs.rs/fn.signal_condition.html)- condition
- Signals `condition`against`stack`; free-function form of`ConditionStack::signal`

# sim_lib_pattern - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-pattern/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Pattern behavior for the SIM runtime over the kernel `Shape` protocol.

The kernel defines the `Shape` match/binding protocol; this crate supplies
the concrete pattern organ (algebraic data types, destructuring, match arms,
and exhaustiveness checking) as pattern surfaces over that protocol.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AdtShape](https://docs.rs/struct.AdtShape.html)
- A kernel `Shape``TaggedValue`
- [Algebraic](https://docs.rs/struct.AlgebraicDataType.html)- Data - Type
- A tagged-union type: a named set of variants, each with its own fields.
- [Match](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchArm.html)- Arm
- One arm of a match: a labelled pattern `Shape`
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternField.html)- Field
- A named field of an ADT variant, carrying the kernel `Shape`
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternMatch.html)- Match
- The outcome of a successful `match_value`
- [Tagged](https://docs.rs/struct.TaggedValue.html)- Value
- A constructed ADT value: an ADT name, a variant tag, and named field values.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantConstructor.html)- Constructor
- A callable builder for one ADT variant.
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantDeclaration.html)- Declaration
- One named variant of an `AlgebraicDataType`
- [Variant](https://docs.rs/struct.VariantShape.html)- Shape
- A kernel `Shape`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [destructure_](https://docs.rs/fn.destructure_expr.html)- expr
- Checks `expr`against a single`shape`, returning the kernel`ShapeMatch`
- [destructure_](https://docs.rs/fn.destructure_value.html)- value
- Checks `value`against a single`shape`, returning the kernel`ShapeMatch`
- [exhaustiveness_](https://docs.rs/fn.exhaustiveness_diagnostics.html)- diagnostics
- Returns diagnostics for any `adt`variants not covered by`arms`.
- [match_](https://docs.rs/fn.match_value.html)- value
- Matches `value`against`arms`in order, returning the first that accepts.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_adt_op_key.html)- adt_ - op_ - key
- Returns the operation key for declaring an ADT.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_destructure_op_key.html)- destructure_ - op_ - key
- Returns the operation key for destructuring a value or expression.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_exhaustive_op_key.html)- exhaustive_ - op_ - key
- Returns the operation key for exhaustiveness checking.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_match_op_key.html)- match_ - op_ - key
- Returns the operation key for matching a value against pattern arms.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_op_keys.html)- op_ - keys
- Returns every operation key the pattern organ publishes.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_organ_symbol.html)- organ_ - symbol
- Returns the organ symbol that identifies the pattern surface.
- [pattern_](https://docs.rs/fn.pattern_tag_op_key.html)- tag_ - op_ - key
- Returns the operation key for constructing a tagged value.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_pattern_organ_claims.html)- pattern_ - organ_ - claims
- Publishes the pattern organ and its operation keys as kernel claims.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_pattern_organ_claims_for_lib.html)- pattern_ - organ_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes pattern organ claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.
- [tagged_](https://docs.rs/fn.tagged_value.html)- value
- Downcasts a runtime `Value``TaggedValue`

# sim_lib_sequence - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-sequence/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Sequence behavior for the SIM runtime: lazy, persistent, and transducers.

The kernel defines the operation and object contracts; this crate supplies the concrete sequence organ (lazy sequences, persistent vectors/maps/sets, and transducer pipelines).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/struct.LazySequence.html)- Sequence
- On-demand sequence object driven by a `SequenceProducer`

- Immutable, shareable set object holding canonically distinct elements.
- [Persistent](https://docs.rs/struct.PersistentVector.html)- Vector
- Immutable, shareable vector object backed by a shared slice.
- [Profile](https://docs.rs/struct.ProfileSequence.html)- Sequence
- Sequence object that tags an inner sequence with a language profile.
- [Transducer](https://docs.rs/struct.TransducerPipeline.html)- Pipeline
- An ordered chain of `TransducerStep`

# sim_lib_standard_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Standard distribution core for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the capability, claim, codec, and `ExportRecord`
contracts; this crate supplies the standard-distribution behavior:
capabilities, claims, diff, fidelity, the conformance harness, install,
language-profile support, the lisp codec surface, polyglot/profile support,
and read/construct.

# sim_shape - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-shape/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Shape algebra, comparison, and match-hook helpers.

`sim-shape` supplies concrete `Shape` implementations while the kernel owns
only the open shape protocol.

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use sim_kernel::{Cx, DefaultFactory, Expr, NoopEvalPolicy};
use sim_shape::{
    AnyShape, ExactExprShape, ExprKind, ExprKindShape, HookedShape, Shape,
    ShapeRelationKind, TraceMarkHook, relate_shapes,
};
let mut cx = Cx::new(Arc::new(NoopEvalPolicy), Arc::new(DefaultFactory));
let exact_true = ExactExprShape::new(Expr::Bool(true));
let bool_expr = ExprKindShape::new(ExprKind::Bool);
let relation = relate_shapes(&mut cx, &exact_true, &bool_expr, &[]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(relation.kind, ShapeRelationKind::LeftSubshape);
assert!(relation.proven);
let hooked = HookedShape::new(Arc::new(AnyShape), vec![Arc::new(TraceMarkHook)]);
let matched = hooked.check_expr(&mut cx, &Expr::String("trace me".to_owned())).unwrap();
assert!(matched.accepted);
assert!(matched.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| {
    diagnostic.message.starts_with("shape-hook:mark")
}));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#surface)Surface

The engine is organized into private module groups whose public items are re-exported at the crate root (the modules themselves are not public):

- `primitives`– atomic shapes (- `AnyShape`,- `ExactExprShape`,- `ExprKindShape`,- `ClassShape`,- `NumberValueShape`,- `ListShape`,- `FieldShape`) and the combinators and object-grammar parsers built on them.
- `algebra`– boolean and collection shape algebra:- `AndShape`,- `OrShape`,- `NotShape`,- `RepeatShape`, and- `TableShape`with its field and extra-field policies.
- `compare`– shape comparison and subsumption: normalization (- `normalize_shape`,- `ShapeNormalForm`), relation analysis (- `relate_shapes`,- `ShapeRelation`), and- `VennShapeSet`set reasoning.
- `citizen`– citizen integration: class registration, codec, and construction for shape objects, plus the- `*_class_symbol`accessors.
- `functions`– the callable shape object:- `FunctionObject`,- `FunctionCase`, overload selection, and shape-as-value wrapping.
- `hooks`– match-extension hooks:- `HookedShape`and the- `MatchHook`protocol with the built-in hook implementations.
- `parse`– the shape grammar parser that turns an- `Expr`into a- `Shape`and runs checks against expressions and values.
- `base`– the base shape vocabulary re-exported from the kernel (- `Shape`,- `ShapeMatch`,- `ShapeDoc`,- `Bindings`,- `ShapeReport`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Accept](https://docs.rs/struct.AcceptOnNoDiagnosticsHook.html)- OnNo - Diagnostics - Hook
- Accept hook that repairs quiet rejections with score 1.
- [AndShape](https://docs.rs/struct.AndShape.html)
- Shape that accepts only when every child shape accepts.
- [AnyShape](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyShape.html)
- The total shape that accepts every value and expression.
- [Bindings](https://docs.rs/struct.Bindings.html)
- Captures produced by a successful match: named values and named exprs.
- [Capture](https://docs.rs/struct.CaptureShape.html)- Shape
- A shape that wraps an inner shape and binds the match under a name.
- [Class](https://docs.rs/struct.ClassShape.html)- Shape
- A shape that matches values and expressions of a named class.
- [Discard](https://docs.rs/struct.DiscardOnDiagnosticPrefixHook.html)- OnDiagnostic - Prefix - Hook
- Discard hook that rejects accepted matches containing a diagnostic prefix.
- [Effectful](https://docs.rs/struct.EffectfulShape.html)- Shape
- A shape that marks its inner shape’s matching as effectful.
- [Exact](https://docs.rs/struct.ExactExprShape.html)- Expr - Shape
- A shape that matches one exact expression form.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprKindShape.html)- Kind - Shape
- A shape that matches expressions of a single `ExprKind`
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldShape.html)- Shape
- A shape that matches an object form field by field.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldSpec.html)- Spec
- A single field requirement within a `FieldShape`

- One overload case of a `FunctionObject`

- A callable function object: a named set of shape-typed overload cases with selection driven by case priority and argument match score.
- [Hooked](https://docs.rs/struct.HookedShape.html)- Shape

- [NotShape](https://docs.rs/struct.NotShape.html)
- Shape that accepts when the inner shape rejects.
- [Number](https://docs.rs/struct.NumberValueShape.html)- Value - Shape
- A shape that matches number-domain values and number expressions.
- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectExpr.html)- Expr
- The decoded form of an object expression: a class symbol and its fields.

- A shape that matches if any one of its choice shapes matches.
- [OrShape](https://docs.rs/struct.OrShape.html)
- Shape that accepts when at least one child shape accepts.

- A shape that parses a string expression with a `ShapeExprParser`
- [Repeat](https://docs.rs/struct.RepeatShape.html)- Shape
- Shape for homogeneous list-like values and collection expressions.
- [Score](https://docs.rs/struct.ScoreFloorHook.html)- Floor - Hook
- Annotate hook that raises accepted match scores to a minimum floor.
- [Selected](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectedCase.html)- Case
- The case chosen by overload selection together with its match result.
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeBindings.html)- Bindings
- Captures produced by a successful match: named values and named exprs.
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeDoc.html)- Doc
- Human-facing description of a `Shape`

- The outcome of checking a value or expr against a `Shape`
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeNormalForm.html)- Normal - Form
- Structural summary used by conservative shape comparison.
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeObject.html)- Object
- Runtime object wrapping a `Shape`
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeRelation.html)- Relation
- Conservative relation report between two shapes.
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeReport.html)- Report
- The canonical record of a shape check: who was checked against what, the outcome, and the diagnostics.
- [Shape](https://docs.rs/struct.ShapeWitness.html)- Witness
- Result of checking one probe against both compared shapes.
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.TableFieldSpec.html)- Field - Spec
- One field constraint inside a `TableShape`
- [Table](https://docs.rs/struct.TableShape.html)- Shape
- Shape for table values or map expressions with named field constraints.
- [Trace](https://docs.rs/struct.TraceMarkHook.html)- Mark - Hook
- Mark hook that emits the wrapped shape label before and after matching.
- [Venn](https://docs.rs/struct.VennShapeSet.html)- Shape - Set
- Named set of shapes used to build Venn-style regions.

# sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/target-redirect/sim_lib_lang_scheme/

## Expand description

Scheme (R7RS-small) surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Scheme surface syntax over the
shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Located](https://docs.rs/struct.LocatedSchemeLowering.html)- Scheme - Lowering
- A `SchemeLowered`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeBaseExport.html)- Base - Export
- A Scheme base-library export: a surface symbol and its description.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodec.html)- Codec
- Decoder turning Scheme surface text into the shared `Expr`graph.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodecLib.html)- Codec - Lib
- Loadable `Lib``SchemeCodec`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeFormSpec.html)- Form - Spec
- Specification of one R7RS-small surface form: its symbol, doc, match shape, and support status.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeFormStatus.html)- Form - Status
- Whether a Scheme surface form is supported by this profile.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeLowered.html)- Lowered
- Result of lowering a Scheme `Expr`to a runtime value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Decodes Scheme surface text into a located `Expr`tree under codec budgets.
- [diagnose_](https://docs.rs/fn.diagnose_unsupported_forms.html)- unsupported_ - forms
- Collects diagnostics for any deferred R7RS-small forms reachable in `expr`.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_r7rs_small_profile.html)- r7rs_ - small_ - profile
- Installs the R7RS-small profile into a `ProfileRegistry`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_expr.html)- scheme_ - expr
- Lowers a single Scheme `Expr`to a`SchemeLowered`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Lowers a located Scheme tree, preserving its origin.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scheme_source.html)- scheme_ - source
- Parses one top-level Scheme form from source text into a located `Expr`tree.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims
- Publishes idempotent base-export card claims for the supported forms.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims_for_lib.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes base-export card claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.

# sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_scheme/index.html

## Expand description

Scheme (R7RS-small) surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Scheme surface syntax over the
shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Located](https://docs.rs/struct.LocatedSchemeLowering.html)- Scheme - Lowering
- A `SchemeLowered`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeBaseExport.html)- Base - Export
- A Scheme base-library export: a surface symbol and its description.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodec.html)- Codec
- Decoder turning Scheme surface text into the shared `Expr`graph.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeCodecLib.html)- Codec - Lib
- Loadable `Lib``SchemeCodec`
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/struct.SchemeFormSpec.html)- Form - Spec
- Specification of one R7RS-small surface form: its symbol, doc, match shape, and support status.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeFormStatus.html)- Form - Status
- Whether a Scheme surface form is supported by this profile.
- [Scheme](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeLowered.html)- Lowered
- Result of lowering a Scheme `Expr`to a runtime value.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Decodes Scheme surface text into a located `Expr`tree under codec budgets.
- [diagnose_](https://docs.rs/fn.diagnose_unsupported_forms.html)- unsupported_ - forms
- Collects diagnostics for any deferred R7RS-small forms reachable in `expr`.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_r7rs_small_profile.html)- r7rs_ - small_ - profile
- Installs the R7RS-small profile into a `ProfileRegistry`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_expr.html)- scheme_ - expr
- Lowers a single Scheme `Expr`to a`SchemeLowered`
- [lower_](https://docs.rs/fn.lower_scheme_tree.html)- scheme_ - tree
- Lowers a located Scheme tree, preserving its origin.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_scheme_source.html)- scheme_ - source
- Parses one top-level Scheme form from source text into a located `Expr`tree.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims
- Publishes idempotent base-export card claims for the supported forms.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_scheme_base_claims_for_lib.html)- scheme_ - base_ - claims_ - for_ - lib

# install_r7rs_small_profile in sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_scheme/fn.install_r7rs_small_profile.html

```
pub fn install_r7rs_small_profile(
    cx: &mut
```
[Cx](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/env/core/struct.Cx.html),
    registry: &mut [ProfileRegistry](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_standard_core/registry/struct.ProfileRegistry.html),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/error/type.Result.html)<[LanguageProfile](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_standard_core/profile/struct.LanguageProfile.html)>## Expand description

Installs the R7RS-small profile into a [ ProfileRegistry](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_standard_core/registry/struct.ProfileRegistry.html), publishing its
base-export card claims.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use sim_kernel::{Cx, DefaultFactory, NoopEvalPolicy};
use sim_lib_standard_core::ProfileRegistry;
use sim_lib_lang_scheme::install_r7rs_small_profile;
let mut cx = Cx::new(Arc::new(NoopEvalPolicy), Arc::new(DefaultFactory));
let mut registry = ProfileRegistry::new();
let profile = install_r7rs_small_profile(&mut cx, &mut registry).unwrap();
assert!(!profile.unsupported_forms.is_empty());
```

# lower_scheme_expr in sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

`pub fn lower_scheme_expr(expr: &`[Expr](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/expr/enum.Expr.html)) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/error/type.Result.html)<[SchemeLowered](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeLowered.html)>## Expand description

# r7rs_small_profile in sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_scheme/fn.r7rs_small_profile.html

`pub fn r7rs_small_profile() -> `[LanguageProfile](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_standard_core/profile/struct.LanguageProfile.html)## Expand description

Builds the R7RS-small [ LanguageProfile](https://docs.rs/sim-lib-standard-core/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_lib_standard_core/profile/struct.LanguageProfile.html): reader, lowering, eval policy,
organ uses, numeric tower, conformance test, fidelity badge, and the
unsupported-form set.

The fidelity badge marks the profile as `standard/partial`: some R7RS-small
forms (see [ r7rs_small_form_specs](https://docs.rs/fn.r7rs_small_form_specs.html)) are
deferred. See the crate

[README](https://docs.rs/crate/sim-lib-lang-scheme)for the language-profile role.

pub struct LanguageProfile {

    pub organs: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[OrganUse](https://docs.rs/struct.OrganUse.html)>,

    pub capabilities: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[CapabilityName](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/capability/struct.CapabilityName.html)>,

    pub conformance_tests: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Symbol](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/id/struct.Symbol.html)>,
    pub fidelity_badges: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[FidelityBadge](https://docs.rs/fidelity/struct.FidelityBadge.html)>,
}## Expand description

A language profile: the reader, lowering, eval-policy, organs, and metadata
that present one surface language over the shared `Expr` graph.

Profiles are the unit the standard distribution installs, diffs, and tests;
the per-language `sim-lib-lang-*` crates build one each.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sim_kernel::Symbol;
use sim_lib_standard_core::{LanguageProfile, OrganUse, standard_control_organ_symbol};
let profile = LanguageProfile::new(Symbol::qualified("lang", "demo/v1"))
    .with_reader(Symbol::qualified("codec", "lisp"))
    .with_eval_policy(Symbol::qualified("eval", "default"))
    .with_organ(OrganUse::new(standard_control_organ_symbol()));
assert_eq!(profile.reader, Symbol::qualified("codec", "lisp"));
assert_eq!(profile.organs.len(), 1);
```

# run_r7rs_small_restricted in sim_lib_lang_scheme - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-scheme/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_scheme/fn.run_r7rs_small_restricted.html

```
pub fn run_r7rs_small_restricted(
    cx: &mut
```
[Cx](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/env/core/struct.Cx.html),
    source: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/error/type.Result.html)<[SchemeLowered](https://docs.rs/enum.SchemeLowered.html)>## Expand description

Decodes and lowers Scheme `source` under untrusted, restricted capabilities.

Rejects any deferred form (e.g. `eval`) with an error before lowering.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use sim_kernel::{Cx, DefaultFactory, NoopEvalPolicy};
use sim_lib_lang_scheme::run_r7rs_small_restricted;
let mut cx = Cx::new(Arc::new(NoopEvalPolicy), Arc::new(DefaultFactory));
assert!(run_r7rs_small_restricted(&mut cx, "(begin #t #f)").is_ok());
assert!(run_r7rs_small_restricted(&mut cx, "(eval '(+ 1 2))").is_err());
```

# a3s 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/a3s/latest

# a3s

The umbrella CLI for the [A3S](https://github.com/A3S-Lab) platform.

`a3s <tool> [args...]` runs the matching A3S tool. `a3s box ...` proxies to
`a3s-box ...` and bootstraps the Box runtime automatically if it is missing:

```
a3s code            # → a3s-code   (launches its TUI)
a3s box ps          # → a3s-box ps (auto-installs a3s-box if needed)
a3s <tool> --help   # a tool's own help
a3s list            # list installed a3s-* tools
a3s --version
```
## Install

```
# from source
# or from this repo
# or Homebrew
```
Then run the tools you need. `a3s box ...` installs `a3s-box` on first use.

## Account Models

In `a3s code`, `/model` lists configured `config.acl` models plus signed-in
account tabs. When Claude Code is logged in (`claude /login`), the Claude Code
tab can switch the current session to Claude models using the local Claude Code
OAuth credentials, including Claude Code's macOS Keychain entry.
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` can also provide the account
token for non-standard environments. If Anthropic rejects the raw OAuth Messages
API bridge with a rate-limit or authentication error, a3s falls back to the
installed `claude` CLI in safe streaming mode; Claude Code's own tools stay
disabled while a3s host tools are requested through an adapter protocol and
still execute inside a3s-code. The adapter accepts Claude Code-style
`<function_calls>` output and tool names such as `Read` or `Bash`, normalizes
common argument aliases like `path` to a3s's `file_path`, and feeds tool results
back into the next Claude turn as structured history.

## Testing

```
```
The ignored soak test repeats `a3s box` after a fake first-use install and
verifies later runs reuse the installed `a3s-box`. The ignored
`ctx_compact_real_llm` test drives the configured model (`~/.a3s/config.acl`)
until the context crosses the auto-compact threshold and asserts streaming
usage is reported, compaction shrinks the history, and the next prompt drops —
the machinery behind the TUI's ctx%, fill warnings, and auto-compaction.

## Updating

In the TUI, ** /update** upgrades to the latest release and restarts into your
session — Homebrew installs are refreshed + upgraded; standalone installs swap
the binary directly. Both paths verify the installed binary reports the target
version before treating the update as successful.

If you're on an **older build (≤ 0.5.4)** whose `/update` was broken, it can't
upgrade itself, and `brew upgrade a3s` alone won't see the new version (Homebrew
doesn't re-sync a tap on `upgrade`). Bootstrap onto a current build once with:

```
 &&
```
From 0.5.5 onward, `/update` handles the tap refresh itself, so this manual step
isn't needed again.

## License

MIT

# a3s 0.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/a3s/0.6.0/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# a3s-code-core 4.2.9 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/a3s-code-core/=4.2.9

A3S Code Core Library

Harness-driven runtime for coding agents.

`Agent` and `AgentSession` are the primary 2.0 API. Lower-level session
runtime state is internal; persistence data flows through `store::SessionData`.

## Quick Start

```
use ;
# async
```
## Disposable Workers

```
use ;
# async
```
## Architecture

```
Agent (config-driven facade)
  +-- AgentSession (workspace-bound execution API)
      +-- internal turn runner
      +-- ContextAssembler / ContextProvider
      +-- ToolSelector
      +-- ToolExecutor
      +-- ProgramExecutor (PTC)
      +-- SkillRegistry
      +-- Permission / confirmation
      +-- Trace / artifacts / verification evidence
Advanced infrastructure:
  +-- optional lane queues for explicit external/hybrid dispatch
```

# a3s-memory 0.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/a3s-memory/^0.1.1

# a3s-memory

Pluggable memory storage for A3S.

Provides the `MemoryStore` trait and two default implementations. Agents that need to persist and recall knowledge across sessions depend on this crate directly — nothing else required.

## Design

The crate follows a minimal core + external extensions pattern:

**Core (stable, non-replaceable):**

- `MemoryStore`— storage backend trait
- `MemoryItem`— the unit of memory
- `MemoryType`— episodic / semantic / procedural / working
- `RelevanceConfig`— scoring parameters

**Extensions (replaceable via  MemoryStore):**

- `InMemoryStore`— default, ephemeral (testing and non-persistent use)
- `FileMemoryStore`— persistent, atomic writes, in-memory index

Three-tier session memory (`AgentMemory`) and context injection (`MemoryContextProvider`) live in `a3s-code`, not here. This crate only owns the storage layer.

## Usage

```
[]
 = {  = "0.1",  = "../memory" }
```
### Store and retrieve

```
use ;
use Arc;
let store = new;
let item = new
    .with_importance
    .with_tag
    .with_type;
store.store.await?;
let results = store.search.await?;
```
### Persistent storage

```
use ;
let store = new.await?;
// Directory layout:
//   memory/
//     index.json        ← in-memory index, persisted atomically
//     items/{id}.json   ← one file per memory item
```
### Custom backend

Implement `MemoryStore` to use any storage system (SQLite, vector DB, etc.):

```
use ;
```
## Relevance scoring

```
score = importance × importance_weight + decay × recency_weight
decay = exp(−age_days / decay_days)
```
Default: `importance_weight = 0.7`, `recency_weight = 0.3`, `decay_days = 30`.

```
use ;
let config = RelevanceConfig ;
let score = item.relevance_score_at;
```
## What this crate does NOT own

| Concern | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Three-tier session memory (working / short-term / long-term) | `a3s-code` |
| `MemoryConfig`(max_short_term, max_working) | `a3s-code` |
| `MemoryStats` | `a3s-code` |
| Context injection into agent prompts | `a3s-code` |

## Tests

32 tests covering `MemoryItem`, `RelevanceConfig`, `InMemoryStore`, and `FileMemoryStore` (including persistence, index rebuild, and path traversal prevention).
